# Color preference study

## Replicate Roy et al. 2025

### Research question

Do pet dogs in the U.S. prefer the color yellow?

![](media/color_bowls_linus.png){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Brown and white dog sitting behind grey, yellow, and blue bowls."}


## Methods

![](media/bowls_color.jpg){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Brown and white dog sitting behind grey, yellow, and blue bowls."}

* Tested 214 dogs under 7 years old at dog parks etc.
* Chose between grey, yellow, and blue bowls
<!-- * Some subjects with food, others without -->
* Recorded first bowl approached


## Dogs preferred yellow

![](media/color_overall.png){.absolute top=120 left=0 height=500 fig-alt="Plot of number of subjects for each bowl color showing stronger preference for yellow over blue."}

![](media/color_yellow_linus2.png){.absolute top=120 left=600 height=500 fig-alt="Brown and white dog sitting with nose in yellow bowl."}


<!-- ## No effect of food present/absent

![](media/color_food2.png){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Plot of number of subjects choosing blue, grey, and yellow bowls with separate panels for with and without food."}


## No sex differences

![](media/color_sex_overall.png){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Plot of number of subjects choosing blue, grey, and yellow bowls with separate panels for males and females."}


## No breed differences

![](media/color_breed_overall.png){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Plot of number of subjects choosing blue, grey, and yellow bowls with separate panels for purebred and mixed breed dogs."}


## No weather differences

![](media/color_weather_overall.png){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Plot of number of subjects choosing blue, grey, and yellow bowls with separate panels for cloudy, rainy, and sunny weather."} -->


## Other factors

No difference in color preference between:

* Males/females
* Purebreeds/mixed breeds
* Cloudy/sunny weather


## Position preferences

![](media/position_overall.png){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Plot of number of subjects chooseing blue, grey, and yellow bowls with separate panels for purebred and mixed breed dogs."}

## But what else might cause preference?

![](media/royetal2025_setup_bowls.jpg){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Image of wooden tray with blue, yellow, and grey bowls."}

![](media/bowls_color_cropped.jpg){.absolute top=250 left=175 width=700 fig-alt="Image of wooden tray with blue, yellow, and grey bowls."}

![](media/bowls_color_filter_cropped.png){.absolute top=450 left=175 width=700 fig-alt="Image of wooden tray with blue, yellow, and grey bowls using a filter for dog vision."}


# Brightness preference study

## Methods

![](media/bowls_grey.jpg){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Illustration of light, medium, and grey bowl."}

* 141 dogs under 7 at dog parks, bars, and daycares
* Chose between light, medium, and dark grey bowls


## Dogs didn't prefer light grey

![](media/color3.png){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Plot of number of subjects choosing light, medium, and dark grey bowls showing slight preference for dark bowls."}


# Wrap up

## Summary

::::{.columns}
:::{.column}
:::{.incremental}
* Young pet dogs in the U.S. prefer the color yellow

* Brightness can't account for this preference
:::
:::
:::{.column}
